runs.answer: 62 different people walked through the shopping centre corridor (phone-68) between 9:44 and 9:54am on 2 Nov — the full recorded clip 09:44:10 to 09:53:38. This is the count of 62 re-identified person identities joining 416 track fragments in that window (48 noted as customers and 14 as staff). Instantaneous occupancy is much lower (~6-10 at once). Confidence is high — identities are the reliable unique-visitor measure here; track counts would over-count by ~7x.

numbers.name: people (visits) who walked through the corridor

runs.answer:
About 14 people went into a shop from the corridor (all into the shops on the left side; the right side is railing/stairs with no shops) during the recorded corridor period 09:44-09:53 UTC on 2026-11-02: ~6 between 09:44:10-09:47:10, ~2 between 09:47:07-09:50:10, and ~6 individuals in 5 entry events between 09:50:07-09:53:10.
Watched the full corridor video in 3 clips and counted each person seen turning off the walkway through the glass shop-front doorway and disappearing inside, excluding passers-by and window-lookers; last ~30s 09:53:10-09:53:39 was not covered and one far pair was low-resolution, so treat 14 as best estimate, moderate-high confidence.

runs.answer:
On the shopping centre corridor camera (phone-68, 09:44-09:53 UTC on 2 Nov 2026, ~9.5 min recording):

- Average time a person stayed in view: ~174 seconds (~2.9 minutes), across 62 person identities.
- Longest stay: ~568 seconds (~9.5 minutes) – essentially the whole recording, first seen 09:44:10 to last seen 09:53:38.

The longest-stayer was a customer adult in a red/maroon upper garment with dark trousers, walking through the corridor with no bag/trolley visible.

How I got it: averaged identity_spans.seconds for concept='person' on phone-68 and took the MAX; role/description from identity_notes. High confidence – based on appearance re-ID identities, not fragmented track IDs; the longest identity has 40 fragments and 225s actually detected.

runs.answer: The corridor was busiest at about 21:49 on 2026-11-02 (phone-93 view looking down the mall). At that peak instant 12 person tracks were in view at the same timestamp (2026-11-02T21:49:02Z). That is about 769 minutes after 9:00 am. Found by counting simultaneous person tracks per timestamp across all corridor cameras, peak = 12 at 21:49, checked with visual count (10-12 visible, SAM found 10 high-confidence plus far small figures) and track-box listing. High confidence that this is the busiest recorded moment.

runs.answer:
On average about 4.8 people – about 5 – were visible in the shopping centre corridor (phone-68) at any one time on 2026-11-02 09:44-09:53 UTC.

How I got it: counted distinct tracked `person` objects per timestamp in track_points for phone-68: 5,301 detections over 1,108 keyframes = 4.78 per frame, median 5, range 1-10. Spot check with a second detector (person counts of 8, 4, 1 at three sample times) confirms low-single-digit typical occupancy. High confidence – continuous 9.5 min coverage.

Around 9:49am on Nov 2 in the shopping centre corridor (phone-68) it was quiet / low-traffic with steady through-flow, no incident.

What was seen 09:48:51-09:49:22 UTC:
- 4-6 people visible at once, moving in both directions, mainly toward the camera. No queue, no shopping carts/trolleys, no staff clearly identifiable.
- Main subjects: a pair walking together toward the camera - woman in brown/tan top with shoulder bag and dark trousers + man in dark jacket/trousers. They paused/slowed briefly by the right-hand pillar/railing/bin area around 09:48:52-09:49:00, then continued together past the camera.
- Following them: a woman in white top/dark trousers walking alone toward the camera, hand to ear as if on phone.
- A man in dark clothing/suit standing stationary by the right pillar/railing near the camera looking at phone, remaining there through the period.
- 2 figures in far distance walking in background.
- No one stopped to look at shop windows on the left, no one entered/exited a shop, no groups beyond that one pair, nothing unusual.

How found: captions for phone-68 09:48:51 and 09:49:12 clips + Spark watch of 09:47:58-09:51:00 video + Glimmer still at 09:49:00 showing 6 boxes. High confidence - three sources agree the corridor was calm with only that pair + 2-3 singles.

In the shopping centre corridor (phone-68, 09:44-09:53 UTC on 2026-11-02) most people walked alone. Movement-checked video review of the full ~9 min in 3 clips found 9 distinct groups of 2 or more people walking together side-by-side in the same direction:

- Clip 09:44-09:47: 5 groups - 2x dark jackets toward camera, 2x long coats (tan/grey) toward camera pausing at window, 2x dark jackets away, 2x foreground (brown jacket + dark jacket) toward camera, 2x suits toward camera.
- Clip 09:47-09:50: +3 new groups - 2x casual (tan top + black jacket) toward camera pausing at railing, 3x (white jacket + brown striped + red/black jacket) from left store toward camera, 3x (red/black jacket + dark coat/green top + dark jacket/scarf) abreast toward camera. One suit-pair is continuation from previous clip.
- Clip 09:50-09:53: +1 new group - 2x (striped sweater + brown sweater) away shoulder-to-shoulder at ~09:52:19. The foreground trio at ~09:50:11 is continuation of the previous 3-person group.

Cross-checked with still frames showing 3-together toward camera at 09:47 and 09:50, and identity overlaps. Confidence medium-high; brief 17s gap at ~09:50:40 not recorded.

Shopping centre corridor (phone-68) on 2026-11-02 09:44-09:53 UTC - very little shop entry/exit, mostly pass-through and window stops:

1. ENTERED left-hand shop at ~09:45:11 UTC - 1 person confirmed:
Man in light beige / off-white jacket and brown trousers. Walked from centre foreground to the left shop-front window/door and disappeared inside the shop. No exit seen in the clip. Walked alone, carrying nothing obvious.

2. Possibly EXITED left-hand shop at ~09:44:17-09:44:21 UTC - 1 person, lower confidence:
Man in dark suit / business jacket with light shirt, right hand to face as if on phone call. Appeared at the very left edge by the shop line in the foreground and walked diagonally across to exit bottom of frame, continuing down the corridor. No other doorway activity in that 12s clip.

All other figures described in captions and video as only stopping at the left glazing to look, not going in:
- Woman in long light-tan coat, blue jeans, shoulder bag + older man in long grey overcoat with dark item - stood together facing glass ~09:45:07-09:45:17, woman touched/pointed at glass, then both walked toward camera together.
- Man in teal shirt with maroon vest and dark trousers - stopped and leaned to glass further down corridor ~09:45:30.
- Person in dark jacket + light trousers further down - stood facing glass looking in.
- Man in brown long-sleeve top/trousers stood by left shopfront ~09:52:53-09:53:03 looking at window/waiting, did not enter.
- Person in red-green vest over teal shirt ~09:51:26 paused to look at window then continued.

How found: searched all phone-68 captions for enter/exit/shop/store/window/door (28 clips, almost all state "no one stops/enters"), then watched 09:45:07-09:45:40 and 09:44:16-09:44:28 clips and checked stills + identity notes for clothing. Confidence high for the 1 entry at 09:45:11, medium for the 09:44:17 exit as he appears at frame edge.

Around 9:48-9:51 am on Nov 2 in the shopping centre corridor (phone-68) it was a quiet, normal low-traffic period - no queues, no carts/trolleys and no staff clearly visible. About 4-5 people were in view at 9:49:00, rising to ~7 by 9:49:30-9:50:00, with ~17 different visitors passing through in the ~3-min 09:48-09:51 window. Flow was in both directions, including a pair walking together and two groups of 3 walking together. One person in a light top entered a shop doorway on the left at ~09:48:06, one person stopped to look into a left-hand shop window for ~7s at ~09:49:34, and 1-2 people lingered briefly at the right-hand railing/bin area on phones. Nothing unusual occurred.

Most visitors walked alone, but groups walking together were common.

Across 6 sampled 3-minute corridor clips I watched (morning 09:44-09:47 on the corridor, plus evening 21:00-21:03, 21:24-21:27, 21:43-21:46, 21:55-21:58 and 22:00-22:03) I counted 14 distinct groups of 2+ walking together:
- 09:44 clip: 5 groups - all pairs, e.g. tan-coat + grey-coat pair who pause to talk, brown-jacket + blazer pair, dark-suit + dark-jacket pair
- 21:24 clip: 1 group - red-top + dark-clothing pair walking away
- 21:43 clip: 3 groups - dark-suit pair, tan-top + dark-jacket pair, trio in white / striped / dark-red-teal jackets
- 21:55 clip: 2 groups - dark-jackets pair away, brown-jacket + dark-jacket pair toward camera
- 22:00 clip: 2 groups - dark-coats pair in distance, tan-coat + grey-coat pair who also linger together at the left shop window
- 21:00 atrium clip: 1 group - white-top + camo-top pair

Single walkers were also seen in every clip, so traffic was a mix of alone and together. The same-looking pairs re-appear in different time windows, so 14 is groups seen in the samples, not necessarily 14 unique visitor parties for the whole day.

Around 9:49 am on 2 Nov in the shopping centre corridor (phone-68) it was very quiet, low-traffic normal passing-through - no queue, no carts, no disorder.

What was visible 09:48-09:51:
- Typically 1-4 people in view at once, up to ~6-7 in one frame at ~09:49:30. Movement both ways, mostly toward the camera, steady walking with gaps when the corridor was empty.
- Groups walking together: a pair - woman in brown/tan top with shoulder bag + man in dark jacket - walking south together toward camera, briefly pausing together by the right pillar / bin / railing then continuing; and a loose group of 3 behind them - white jacket, striped sweater, red/green top - and later a 3-man group - red jacket, dark coat/green shirt, brown jacket - walking side-by-side conversing.
- Window / shop activity: No clear shop entry. One person in grey tracksuit stopped at left glass front ~09:49:32 for ~7-8s leaning to look inside then walked on; pair briefly looked over right railing; one man in dark suit walked north on phone then leaned against right railing/pillar by the bin for ~15-20s before leaving south.
- No queues, no staff clearly identifiable, no running/crowding.

Note: video overlay shows old 20-01-2004 timecode and jumps around 09:50:40-09:50:57, so it is not fully continuous, but all sources agree - calm transit with brief browsing/pauses.

How found: captions for phone-68 09:44-09:53, watch of 09:48:00-09:51:00 clip, and look at 09:48:30, 09:49:30, 09:50:30. Confidence high - three methods agree.
